# Agent permission harness — findings

2 findings across 1 workflow files — 1 defects and 1 posture records. All 2 are decided from the workflow artifact with nothing running; 1 of them would *also* be visible to an attack-replay harness pointed at the running agent, and none require one.

## How this can be wrong

Measured against 34 synthetic fixture cases in this probe's own test suite (author-authored to isolate each rule, not an independent or held-out corpus): 0 false positives, 0 false negatives on the 16/34 positive-rule opportunities those fixtures cover across all seven rules (R1-R7). This is a floor on precision and recall, not an out-of-sample estimate: every fixture was written already knowing which rule it was meant to trip.

Two things follow from how the rules are built, and both matter more than the fixture count above.

**Zero false positives is a design property confirmed, not guaranteed.** Every one of the seven rules fires only on structural, positively-named evidence in the workflow artifact -- a script reference that does not resolve, a fixed delimiter, an untrusted expression spliced into a script, a mutable action ref, an inherited scope, a write-holding agent step, a prompt whose named reads resolve to files. No rule infers a defect from an *absence* of evidence. That is why zero false positives held on every fixture built to test it -- it is what the design predicts -- but 34 author-authored fixtures confirm the design on the cases it was built for, not on production workflow files this probe has never seen.

**False negatives on attack classes none of the seven rules encode are real and unmeasured.** The fixture corpus only tests whether *coded* rules (R1-R7) behave correctly on cases *designed to exercise them*. It says nothing about a misconfiguration or injection shape none of the seven encodes -- that produces no finding at all, silently, and this corpus cannot rule it out because it was never asked to. R5 and R6 are posture records, not defect calls, so a false positive there would not mean "wrongly flagged an attacker path" the way it would for R1-R4 or R7; they are included in the count above on the narrower, honest claim that each fires exactly when its own documented structural condition is present, which is the only accuracy claim posture rules admit.

## R6-agent-holds-write-scope — Agent step holds repository write scope

- **`.github/workflows/opencode-high-throughput.yml` job `opencode-agent` (line 177)** — agent step runs with contents, id-token, pull-requests
  - The step invokes an agent while the job holds contents, id-token, pull-requests and token:contents,id-token,pull-requests secrets:GITHUB_TOKEN,OPENCODE_API_KEY. Recorded as the privilege baseline for this file: every reachable input below is reachable *to this*.
  - writer set of the reachable input: `LITERAL`; privilege reached: `token:contents,id-token,pull-requests secrets:GITHUB_TOKEN,OPENCODE_API_KEY`; visible to attack replay: yes

## R7-agent-instruction-closure — Agent instruction set exceeds its prompt input

- **`.github/workflows/opencode-high-throughput.yml` job `opencode-agent` (line 116)** — agent instruction set is 311 repository files, not the 1 prompt file(s) passed to it
  - The prompt handed to this agent directs it to read and heed `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `portfolio/DIRECTION.md`, `portfolio/pipeline/README.md`, `review_pending.py` -- which resolve to 5 files in this checkout. Those files order further reads of their own, and the fixed point of that is 311 files (5 at depth 1, 213 at depth 2, 40 at depth 3, 53 at depth 4), among them `.github/workflows/agent-cross-review.yml`, `.github/workflows/agent-pr-auto-merge.yml`, `.github/workflows/claude-routine-trigger.yml`, `.github/workflows/garmin-world-traveler-watchface-ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/hetzner-gitops-ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/pages.yml`. Every one is an ordinary repository file with writer set REPO_WRITE, and the agent reads them while holding token:contents,id-token,pull-requests secrets:GITHUB_TOKEN,OPENCODE_API_KEY. Hardening or replaying attacks against the prompt input alone leaves this surface untested. The count is an upper bound on what the prompt directs (a named path is counted whether the naming document orders the read or merely mentions the file) and a lower bound on the surface (only prose is walked through, so a path named solely inside a data file in the closure is missed).
  - writer set of the reachable input: `REPO_WRITE`; privilege reached: `token:contents,id-token,pull-requests secrets:GITHUB_TOKEN,OPENCODE_API_KEY`; visible to attack replay: no
